issues.legal_issue: A grantee with limited rights to fell and use trees does not acquire absolute ownership of the trees or an unrestricted right to remove timber from the granted land.
material_facts: The grant and related agreement allowed the grantee to use timber within the granted area, subject to specified limits on felling.
The agreement prohibited carrying unworked timber or articles made from it outside the granted area except in accordance with the forest and customs rules in force.
The company sought free passes to transport timber felled in the area beyond its limits.
issues.conclusion: The company did not acquire absolute proprietary rights over the trees and timber or an unrestricted right to remove them; the State was justified in refusing free transportation outside the granted area.
issues.legal_principle: The court interpreted the grant and ratification documents, particularly clause 7 of the 1886 agreement and clause 5 of the ratification deed, as limiting the grantee to felling and using timber for specified purposes within the granted area. It agreed with the interpretation of the analogous clause in George A. Leslie v. State of Kerala, [1969] KLT 378, that permission to appropriate timber within the grant indicated a concession to the grantee, not a transfer of absolute ownership.

predicates.state_appeal_from_decree: The State appealed a decree concerning the grantee’s claimed rights over trees or timber.
predicates.grant_limits_tree_use: The grant allowed the grantee to fell or use trees only within specified purposes or limits.
predicates.grant_conditions_external_transport: The grant made removal of timber beyond the granted area subject to applicable rules.
predicates.grantee_lacks_absolute_tree_ownership_an: The grantee does not own the trees absolutely or have an unrestricted right to remove the timber.

issues.definition: When the State appeals a decree and the grant limits tree use and conditions external transport on applicable rules, the grantee lacks absolute tree ownership and unrestricted removal rights.

issues.legal_issue: The government may demand Kuttikanam for timber removed from granted land when the government owns the tree growth and applicable rules authorize the levy.
material_facts: The court found that ownership of the tree growth and timber remained with the Government, while the grantee had only limited rights to fell and use timber.
The agreement required external transport of timber to conform to forest rules in force.
Rules made under the Travancore-Cochin Forest Act, 1951 regulated Kuttikanam on trees standing on Government land and were in force at the relevant time.
The Kerala Forest Act, 1961 repealed the earlier Act but saved rules made under it.
issues.conclusion: The State was empowered to levy and demand Kuttikanam for timber taken out of the granted area.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 93(2)(d), (dd) and (e) of the Travancore-Cochin Forest Act, 1951, rules could regulate Kuttikanam on trees standing on Government land. The relevant rules treated trees reserved to the Government under a grant as Government property and provided for payment when Government timber was sold to the landholder. Section 85(3) of the Kerala Forest Act, 1961 saved those rules. The court also relied on George A. Leslie v. State of Kerala, [1969] KLT 378, which explained Kuttikanam as the Government’s share of the value of trees it owned, rather than a tax or fee.

rule.if: state_appeal_from_decree and government_owned_tree_growth and timber_removed_beyond_grant and grant_requires_compliance_with_forest_rules and rules_authorize_levy_and_remain_in_force

predicates.state_appeal_from_decree: The State appealed a decree concerning a demand for payment on timber removed from granted land.
predicates.government_owned_tree_growth: The Government retained ownership of the trees or tree growth on the land.
predicates.timber_removed_beyond_grant: The grantee took or sought to take timber beyond the limits of the granted land.
predicates.grant_requires_compliance_with_forest_ru: The grant required external transport of timber to comply with forest rules in force.
predicates.rules_authorize_levy_and_remain_in_force: Applicable rules authorized a levy on Government-owned timber and continued to operate when the timber was removed.

issues.definition: When the State appeals, the Government owns the tree growth, timber is removed beyond the grant, the grant requires compliance with forest rules, and rules in force authorize a levy, the Government may demand a tree-removal levy.

issues.legal_issue: A government communication about seigniorage on timber used within granted land does not bar a levy on timber removed beyond that land.
material_facts: A government letter addressed a dispute about seigniorage on reserved trees used by the company within the granted area.
The letter followed correspondence that raised the question of timber rights in the area but concerned the company’s use of timber within the area.
The agreement clearly subjected external transport of timber to the forest and customs rules in force.
issues.conclusion: The letter could not be read as preventing Kuttikanam from being levied on timber removed beyond the granted area.
issues.legal_principle: The court read the government letter in the context of the correspondence to which it responded and confined it to timber used within the granted area. The clear wording of clause 7 of the agreement governed external transport; the letter was to be interpreted in light of that wording, not used to displace it.

predicates.state_appeal_from_decree: The State appealed a decree in a dispute over payment for timber removed from granted land.
predicates.correspondence_concerned_with_in_grant_u: The government communication addressed payment for timber used within the granted area.
predicates.grant_expressly_conditions_external_tran: The grant expressly made transport of timber beyond its limits subject to applicable rules.
predicates.prior_communication_does_not_bar_levy_on: The earlier communication does not prevent a levy on timber removed beyond the granted area.

issues.definition: When the State appeals, the correspondence concerns timber used within the grant, and the grant expressly conditions external transport, the earlier communication does not bar a levy on timber removed beyond the grant.
